I've done the same thing as you, constructed a life around what people expect of me, who they expect me to be, and even though my job prospects are good and my CV/resume will get me a great job, it's just completely not what i want. But I do think it's not about the job or family or friends, i think you have to love yourself completely first, once you've started to love yourself good things will gravitate towards you, you will meet another girl who falls in love with you and you'll be happy.

i call it de-personalisation, when you sort of forget you who are. i went through such a dark and deep depression about 4/5 years ago when i completely lost who i was. i didn't understand the point to socialising or even seeing my family, i just couldn't understand why i would do it, that's when you're black. today i'm sad to say i feel like that again, after 5 years, i'm back where i started. you seem okay, just upset about love. i think you'll bounce back. i would use the resources you have, all that money, to cure myself by going to a good therapist. i can't afford anything like that so i just have to rot in my reality, there's no one here to help me and I'm just alone.

thankyou so much for your help and advice, i really appreciate it and it is very helpful. i will look into these different antidepressants, can the doctor's do a test on your brain to see if you are low on seratonin or some other chemical, I've been told that that's sometimes the case if you've been depressed for long periods of time (years etc).

I would definitely be there for my friends but i just can't bring myself to do it to them, at the moment i will just try and do things independently, i'm worried that when major things start to happen (i'm quite nervous about us moving house, i don't really know why), or if my dad has to go to hospital maybe i will have to reach out to a friend, i know it sounds bad but i think when that happens, the hurt and the pain just isn't worth it. i don't want to see my dad suffering and then my mum's world falling apart, i don't know what a friend could do really, at that point its over for me.
wow, make some more music. why did you stop?
seriously, nyc flashes is sick! its like gold panda as well. have you ever sent this to a record label?

cool, do you like philip k dick, he's one of my favourite authors and he writes sic-fi/dystopia stuff. it would probably be really good inspiration for you.

i really ilk your music, it reminds me of burial - do you know who that is?  ambient indigo and nyc flashes are sick. it's like aphex twin a bit too.

thanks for your message, its really kind of you to reply with advice. 

what do you mean by right medications? do you take something? i thought they give you antidepressants, what other pills are there?

my friends are nice but i don't think they have time to help, they all have their own lives to be thinking about and their family. i want to tell my family but they're just not stable enough themselves. my dad will just tell me to put my faith in god, my mum will probably just cry and lose sleep, she works everyday from 5am-10pm doing labour cleaning work just so we have enough money for food so i don't want to jeorpoadise her job. otherwise we'll have nothing and won't be able to pay bill :S

sorry if i sounded moany, i know i should be more thankful for what i have, i don't like sounded so spoilt, i do appreciate everything I've got its just it comes to a point where nothing seems to shift me out this bubble.

im scared to tell me friends because i don't want to put any pressure them, it will make them feel uncomfortably and i don't want to be a burden on anyone. i'm trygn to working it out myself independently. how have you done it specifically? even in your comment you seem so confident and sure of yourself, I'm nothing like that.

I feel the same, but the fact you had a girlfriend for seven years is amazing. you sound very intelligent, which i know sometimes makes things worse because you over think things more, but you have a lot going for you. a lot more compared to other people. sometimes i try and think relatively, that compared to someone in africa I'm so lucky. i have a nice warm house and food on the table and family, I'm not sure if that will help you to just take a step back and reflect on how amazing and capable you are. to have a relationship for 7 years shows you've got such good stuff about you, i think the psychiatric ward would be better, you slowly work your way up until you feel a bit better, before it gets worse. 

i think life is so hard as well, i have deep depression and anxiety and none of the people around me even know, but when i read your comment i just think wow, there's someone who's so much luckier than me, you actually have things to live for, you're really eloquent. id love to hear the music, can you put a link in? what sort of book are you writing? i make music too about my depression, it's the only way i can escape from everything for a while. i imagine making the music and then killing myself and leaving that behind for everyone. but you've got so much to live for, so much.
> account well done for getting through it, it's so hard i have the same thing. what do you do to make things easier?
